justification: 5,000 scenarios and physician rubrics were released openly by OpenAI on GitHub, so the exact eval set is scrapable and clinician-conversation style QA is well-represented in medical-web pretraining data.

Questions and gold answers are both public on the GitHub repo/HF dataset, and USMLE-style expert medical reasoning is a well-trodden pretraining genre despite being explicitly built to be harder than MedQA.
MedQA-USMLE questions and answers have been fully public since 2020 and are now considered saturated/contaminated by the field, with GPT-4-class models exceeding 90% via prompting alone.
194K questions drawn from public Indian medical entrance exam prep material with answers included in the public dataset, making it highly susceptible to memorization.
Questions, contexts (PubMed abstracts), and labels are all public; based on standard biomedical literature comprehension, a skill heavily represented in web/PubMed pretraining corpora.

All 162 tasks and answer keys are open on GitHub/HuggingFace (crowd-built via a public workshop); legal issue-spotting/rule-recall over standard doctrine is well represented in web and legal-corpus pretraining, and Vals AI's live tracking layer reruns the same public tasks rather than rotating them.

Derived from public US case law (Harvard's Caselaw Access Project) with holdings and multiple-choice distractors published alongside the dataset; case law is extensively represented in legal pretraining corpora.

FinBen's 36 datasets and evaluation code are open on GitHub (some sub-tasks reuse existing public financial NLP datasets), but a few sub-tasks (e.g. live stock-trading decision simulation) inject genuinely novel sequential-decision structure not just recalled financial trivia.

The public HF release intentionally withholds ~30% of gold answers/evidence to deter contamination, and grounding open-ended answers in specific real 10-K/10-Q filings pushes past generic finance-textbook knowledge, though the filings themselves are public web documents.

Vals AI markets its underlying task sets as private/proprietary enterprise benchmarks with a live leaderboard that adds new models continuously, but exact rotation cadence and task composition are not publicly documented, and composite GDP-weighted domain coverage is not independently verifiable -- treat with caution (see report).

Scale explicitly markets SEAL/PRBench as keeping datasets and gold answers unpublished specifically to resist gaming, with new prompts added over time; professional-reasoning tasks (incl. legal) sit atop generic domain knowledge, limiting true novelty.

Code, environments (EB-ALFRED/EB-Habitat/EB-Navigation/EB-Manipulation), and eval scripts are open on GitHub, but grounding multi-step action sequences in simulated 3D environments has little precedent in generic text pretraining, especially for low-level manipulation.

Both ALFRED (2019) and VirtualHome (2018) publish full task/trajectory data and evaluation code; embodied step-by-step household action sequencing has little representation in generic internet text, though both benchmarks are old enough that derivative walkthroughs/solutions may now be indexed on the web.

ALFWorld (chosen as representative; text/embodied-linked TextWorld environments) publishes full game files and code on GitHub with no held-out answer key since agents are evaluated by live environment interaction, and simulated multi-step household task execution has little generic-pretraining precedent -- though extensive published agent transcripts (ReAct, Reflexion, AgentBench, etc.) mean specific task solutions are increasingly discoverable.
